questions.question: The humerus is classified as a:

explanations.a: The humerus is not classified as a flat bone.
explanations.b: The humerus is not classified as a short bone.
explanations.c: The humerus is a long bone of the upper limb, extending from the shoulder to the elbow.
explanations.d: The humerus is not classified as an irregular bone.

questions.question: The humerus articulates proximally with the:

explanations.a: The clavicle does not directly articulate with the humerus.
explanations.b: The head of the humerus articulates with the glenoid cavity of the scapula to form the shoulder joint.
explanations.c: The radius articulates with the distal end of the humerus at the elbow.
explanations.d: The ulna articulates with the distal end of the humerus at the elbow.

questions.question: The distal end of the humerus articulates with:

explanations.a: The distal humerus articulates with the radius but also articulates with the ulna.
explanations.b: The distal humerus articulates with the ulna but also articulates with the radius.
explanations.c: The distal end of the humerus articulates with both the radius and ulna at the elbow joint.
explanations.d: The scapula does not articulate with the distal end of the humerus.

questions.question: The head of the humerus is directed:

explanations.a: The head of the humerus is not directed downward and lateral.
explanations.b: The head is directed upward, medially and slightly backward.
explanations.c: The head of the humerus is directed upward, medially and backward, allowing it to articulate with the glenoid cavity.
explanations.d: The head is not directed downward and medial.

questions.question: The greater tubercle of the humerus is located:

explanations.a: The greater tubercle is not located medially; the lesser tubercle is positioned more anteriorly and medially.
explanations.b: The greater tubercle has posterior and lateral surfaces but is primarily located laterally.
explanations.c: The greater tubercle is a prominent bony projection located on the lateral aspect of the proximal humerus.
explanations.d: The greater tubercle is not primarily an inferior structure.

questions.question: The intertubercular groove is also known as:

explanations.a: The deltoid tuberosity is a different anatomical structure on the humerus.
explanations.b: The intertubercular groove is also called the bicipital groove because it contains the tendon of the long head of the biceps brachii.
explanations.c: The radial groove is located on the posterior surface of the shaft of the humerus.
explanations.d: The nutrient canal is a separate anatomical feature and is not called the bicipital groove.

questions.question: The trochlea of the humerus articulates with the:

explanations.a: The capitulum of the humerus articulates with the head of the radius.
explanations.b: The trochlea articulates with the trochlear notch of the ulna at the elbow joint.
explanations.c: The scapula articulates with the proximal head of the humerus, not the trochlea.
explanations.d: The clavicle does not articulate with the trochlea.

questions.question: The humerus is important for estimating:

explanations.a: Although some skeletal features can contribute to age assessment, this is not the primary anthropological application referred to here.
explanations.b: The humerus can provide information useful for sex estimation.
explanations.c: Measurements and morphological features of the humerus can be useful in estimating stature and sex in forensic and anthropological studies.
explanations.d: Bones cannot be used to determine an individual's blood group.

questions.question: The nutrient foramen of the humerus is usually directed:

explanations.a: The nutrient canal of the humerus is not usually directed toward the elbow.
explanations.b: The nutrient foramen of the humerus is usually directed proximally, toward the shoulder.
explanations.c: The nutrient foramen is not usually directed toward the hand.
explanations.d: The nutrient canal follows a longitudinal direction rather than being directed horizontally.
